expectations.text: Requests two Operations staff members for eight hours per week over a four-week pilot and gives the 26 April approval deadline and proposed 6 May start.
expectations.evidence: “two Operations staff members for a four-week pilot ... starting 6 May”; “Approval by 26 April”; “those eight hours each week.”

expectations.text: Uses the observed counts accurately: 46 returns, 18 delayed more than two working days, and seven repeat inquiries; does not present them as a complete company-wide baseline or claim a measured time saving.
expectations.evidence: “46 returns, including 18 ... more than two working days”; “Seven employees contacted reception twice”; “they do not measure all returns across the company”; “There is no staff-time baseline.”

expectations.text: Explains the Tuesday/Thursday West Office service and retains the existing reception option outside those hours and locations.
expectations.evidence: “ground-floor service counter on Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.” at West Office; “through reception on other days and at other offices.”

expectations.text: States concrete next-working-day registration and overnight storage measures and a stop/adjust/extend review after week four, without promising the pilot will succeed.
expectations.evidence: “at least 90% ... by the next working day”; “whether any equipment remains outside the cabinet overnight”; “After four weeks ... stopping, adjusting, or extending.” The measures are proposed assessments, not promised results.
